trust_decision.summary: The revocation endpoint treats the client-supplied `callback` request parameter as trusted JavaScript source: with enable_jsonp=True it builds the response body as `callback + '();'` on success and `'{}({});'.format(callback, e.json)` on errors, so a request controls the JS text sent to the browser.

landing_point.why: The advisory names RevocationEndpoint, and the first place a request-controlled string is spliced into a JS response body is the enable_jsonp branch at :72-73.

fix_sites.entry_point: RevocationEndpoint.create_revocation_response (error branch); inherited unchanged by oauthlib.oauth2.Server and the four pre-configured *Server classes
oauthlib.oauth2.rfc6749.parameters.prepare_token_revocation_request (module-level public request builder; the JSONP branch is what moves token params from body to URL query)

oauthlib.oauth2.Client.prepare_token_revocation_request (every client subclass: WebApplicationClient, MobileApplicationClient, LegacyApplicationClient, BackendApplicationClient, ServiceApplicationClient)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The client helper only emits a `callback` parameter and moves the token params into the URL; the arbitrary-JavaScript sink is server-side, so changing the client-library signature is optional API cleanup rather than part of the XSS.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Error responses must keep returning the OAuth2 error JSON together with the error's own headers and status (401 invalid_client with WWW-Authenticate), and the success path must keep 200 with an empty body and still call request_validator.revoke_token; a fix that stops building the response body wholesale (returns '' on error, or drops e.headers) breaks the error contract.

O6_input_shapes: callback supplied in the x-www-form-urlencoded POST body (reaches both the success and the error branch)
callback supplied in the URI query string: _raise_on_bad_post_request rejects it, and the resulting InvalidRequestError is then JSONP-wrapped by the error branch
callback passed as a keyword argument to Client.prepare_token_revocation_request / parameters.prepare_token_revocation_request, which moved the token parameters from the body into the URL query

O8b_injection_room.sibling: enable_jsonp-style wrapping of the introspection JSON body with a client-supplied callback
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: IntrospectEndpoint is the sibling JSON-response endpoint built on the same BaseEndpoint and Request plumbing, so copying the revocation enable_jsonp branch is a one-line change a maintainer could plausibly have made.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: JSONP wrapping of the metadata document
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: create_metadata_response already returns json.dumps(self.claims) with Content-Type: application/json and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so the same format() wrap fits naturally for browser clients.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: callback re-emitted through the generic **kwargs passthrough after the explicit parameter is removed
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the kwargs loop already appends any truthy keyword as a request parameter, so `callback=` survives the signature removal and a maintainer could keep the JSONP behaviour alive through that route instead of deleting the branch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: enable_jsonp on the device-authorization JSON response
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: newer endpoint written against the same BaseEndpoint/Request pattern and JSON response shape, the obvious place to copy a JSONP feature from.

O9_family: CWE-79 reflected cross-site scripting via unvalidated JSONP callback injected into a JavaScript response body

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools (setup.py, python_requires>=3.9) + pip; tox envs run `pytest --cov=oauthlib tests/`
O10_build.project_tests: tests/oauth2/rfc6749/endpoints/test_revocation_endpoint.py (test_revoke_with_callback at :91 asserts the vulnerable wrapping; :30-89 assert the normal and error paths) and tests/oauth2/rfc6749/clients/test_base.py:220-243 (JSONP client block at :240-243); both are pure unittest/mock, no network.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the two enable_jsonp response-body branches in RevocationEndpoint only, leaving the client-side `callback` parameter and the body-vs-URL placement in parameters.py and clients/base.py untouched.

unverified: Repo size in MB not measured (shell disabled); likely small but tiny_repo not asserted.

The published fix's client-side change is signature removal, but the generic **kwargs loop (parameters.py:219-221) still forwards `callback` into the request body, so the post-fix API does not hard-reject it; the published tests only assert the URL no longer carries the callback.
Whether hidden tests require the client-side signature removals (a breaking API change) or only the server-side behaviour is unknown.

`request.callback` is not declared in Request._params (common.py:360-394) and only exists when a callback param is present, so an enable_jsonp endpoint built without a callback parameter raises AttributeError at revocation.py:72; not exercised by the pinned tests.

No pre-configured server passes enable_jsonp (pre_configured.py:92,145,188,239,282; openid pre_configured.py:137), so the vulnerable feature is opt-in and unreachable from the shipped Server classes - the strongest 'reason to dismiss' for the main sink.
O13 recall_risk is a judgement; no write-up search was performed.
